current_prompt.body:
CALCULATE the probability that for a unit-length stick broken at two random points, the ratio of the shortest piece to the longest piece is at least 1/4.
RETURN the result as a simplified fraction.
NOTE that the previously provided answer 13/36 was incorrect and a recomputation is required.

current_plan.body:
DEFINE the geometric model of a unit-length stick broken at two independent uniformly random points
IDENTIFY the ordered break positions as variables X and Y with 0 ≤ X ≤ Y ≤ 1
DERIVE the lengths of the three pieces as L1 = X, L2 = Y‑X, L3 = 1‑Y
DETERMINE the shortest piece S = MIN(L1, L2, L3) and the longest piece L = MAX(L1, L2, L3)
FORMULATE the condition S / L ≥ 1/4 as an inequality region in the (X, Y) plane
SET UP the double integral of the uniform joint density over the region satisfying the inequality
EVALUATE the integral to obtain the probability value
SIMPLIFY the resulting rational number to its lowest terms
OUTPUT the simplified fraction as the final result
